exclude: the loader's text screen, left as it was: spaces, then power-on bytes; the game never shows it

runtime: in play the two pitch screens ($6C00, $7400), the panel's screen ($7000) and the character set ($7800), all built from data held elsewhere ($DF55, $EC0D, the map at $F300); in the menus the bitmap at $6000
runtime: in play the pitch map, 40 columns by 74 rows, which pitch_map_build ($917D) writes; between matches it holds the play sprites, which play_sprites_in ($916A) copies to $5C00

comments.text: The 6510's own data direction register; the disassembler's name for address 0 and the start of zero page.

The processor port: which of RAM, the chips, the KERNAL and BASIC the processor sees. $30 (all RAM) through the game, $0D in the raster interrupt and between io_in and io_out, $36 for the KERNAL's save and load.
Two bytes: the address irq_slot_run jumps through, the current slot's handler. The save code keeps $02-$0D at $BFC0 while the KERNAL runs.
High byte of the slot handler's address.
Two zero page bytes no routine was found to use; the save code keeps them with $02-$0D.
Two bytes the game jumps through (jump_06): the chosen menu entry's handler, a computer player's role routine, a tile's effect, the screen-copy routine for the scroll.
High byte of the jump address.
The raster interrupt's current slot, 0-11: the line, video settings and handler come from the tables at $2C3A-$2C9F. keys_read flips it with $AA when the timer check fails.
ORed into every slot's VIC control register 1: $10 shows the screen, 0 blanks it.
ANDed with every slot's sprite-enable byte: $FF shows the sprites, 0 hides them.
wait_frame sets it to 1 and waits for the interrupt to clear it. frame_work stores $2DD0 there, 0 on a genuine copy; anything else would keep wait_frame waiting for ever.
Port 2's joystick, read each frame: 1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, $10 fire, ORed with $2DD0. Player 1, and the menus.
Port 1's joystick, read each frame and EORed with $2468: player 2 in a two player game.
Counts frames, one a raster interrupt pass of frame_work; the music fade reads it.
Counts down once a frame: the menus' wait for a key, and repeat delays.
Counts down once every 256 frames, about five seconds: the team choice gives up after six.
A source pointer, two bytes, for the copy and drawing routines.
High byte of the source pointer.
A destination pointer, two bytes, for the copy and drawing routines (screen, bitmap or colour RAM).
High byte of the destination pointer.
Two bytes: the packed string text_draw is reading.
High byte of the packed string's address.
A work byte for many routines: a loop counter, a row count, a pair index.
A second work byte: a count, a colour, an OR mask.
Two bytes: the glyph text_draw copies, in the font at $DCDD.
High byte of the glyph's address.
The multiplexer's next entry in the sorted object list $1E-$2D; sprites_place sets it to the number of objects above the panel.
The multiplexer's position at the start of a pass, to tell whether a pass placed any sprite.
Sixteen bytes, $1E-$2D: the objects (players 0-9, launcher 10-13, ball 15) in order of their height on screen, sorted each pass by sprites_sort for the multiplexer.
The second entry of the sorted object list, which sprites_sort compares with the first.
Two bytes: the pitch line at the top of the view, which the scroll follows: the followed object's y less $54, kept between 0 and $1A8 (camera_follow).
High byte of the camera's line.
An object's line on screen, from object_screen_pos: its y less the view's top.
High byte of the object's screen line: not 0 when it is off the view.
Two bytes of the random generator's state, seeded $19, $63 at start-up; random_next shifts and mixes them, and the low byte is the number.
High byte of the random generator's state.
random_range keeps X here.
random_range's lower limit.
random_range's result, brought within the limits.
The 16-bit position the direction routines start from: x at $37/$3B, y at $38/$3C; the target follows at $39/$3D and $3A/$3E, and the differences are left here.
The start position's y low byte (high byte $3C).
The target's x low byte (high byte $3D): where a computer-run player is heading.
The target's y low byte (high byte $3E).
High byte of the start position's x.
High byte of the start position's y.
High byte of the target's x.
High byte of the target's y.
A loop counter: blocks, rows, domes.
A second loop counter: rows of a picture or a frame.
The stick bits being acted on for the current player: the joystick for a human, the computer's choice for the rest (1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, $10 fire).
Two bytes: the mask list the face routines step through (mask_bit_next).

High byte of mask_ptr: the mask list's address for the picture and face copies (mask_bit_next); the team animation at $3E5A also uses $42/$43 as the address of the bitmap it draws to (team_picture_lo/hi).
Which of the two pitch screens is on show: 0 $6C00 or 1 $7400; screen_flip swaps it.
The x difference between two objects (pair_distances, ball_distances, dome_bounce), held to $7F; or a point's x for distance_approx, which leaves the distance here.
The y difference between two objects, held to $7F; or a point's y for distance_approx.
High byte of the x difference, or the second point's x for distance_approx.
High byte of the y difference, or the second point's y for distance_approx.
A work counter: rows, cells, the tackle loop.
The map row at the top of the screen last drawn; $FF forces scroll_update to draw the screen again (after a tile appears or goes).
1 holds the camera where it is (the launcher and the start of a match); 0 lets camera_follow move it.
Set by pair_distances when it has worked out every pair's distance; tackles_check runs only then and clears it.
Two bytes: the camera's line less $36, taken from each object's y to give its sprite's y.
High byte of the sprite offset.
Set when the sprite pointers and colours have changed; irq_slot_panel copies them to the hidden screen's pointers and clears it.
The number of objects in view this pass, from sprites_place.
sound_play keeps X here.
sound_play keeps Y here.
A flag for a tune playing over the match: sound_play would then play no effect, and kick-off would start tune 0. Nothing writes it after the start-up clears zero page, so it is always 0.
Which half of a packed byte the string reader is on.
F3, read each frame: quit the match, back to the menu from the prematch screens.
RUN/STOP, read each frame: pause.
F5, read each frame; nothing in the game reads it.
A 16-bit work value, low byte (high byte $59): a y position for the keeper and the computer's shot, or a player's new y in player_step.
High byte of the work value at $58.
Two bytes: the x step for player_step, from the speed tables at $BA61.
High byte of the x step (the sign).

The current side's fire counter (from $64 or $65, back there after player_move). It moves on only after a throw has started: a press with the ball throws at once (ball_throw) and then each pass with fire held adds one, while human_turn ($5F) is set, and at 5 the throw becomes a high one; $FF marks it done. A press without the ball leaves it at 0.
The direction (0-7) player_dir_step moves the player in: from the stick, or his facing when he is turned away.
Set when the controlled player has fire held without the ball: copied to $1EC0 or $1EC1, the side's edge in a tackle.
1 while the two controlled players are being moved, 0 for the rest; fire acts only in the first.
The side 0 player under control, 0-4: the one nearest the ball, or the one holding it. Starts at 4.
The side 1 player under control, 5-9. Starts at 9.
Counts passes of the match loop: the controlled players' flashing, the computer's timing.
Side 0's fire counter, kept between passes (fire_count).
Side 1's fire counter.
Steps once a pass: the offset tile_step reads the tile's patterns from, so the pattern rolls.
Passes until the next tile appears; 0 while a tile is on the pitch; $FF none (taken, or removed for a goal).
The tile on the pitch: 0 a token, 1-10 the power-ups ($BB21 picks it).
The tile's column on the pitch grid, 2-12 (cells of 16 pixels).
The tile's row on the pitch grid, 2-30.
Power-up P: the side that has it ($FF side 1, 1 side 0, 0 nobody); it protects that side's players from being knocked down.
Power-up F: the opposing side's players stand still.
Power-up R: the opposing side's players move one step slower.
Power-up W: the ball becomes the electric one, and the opponents who touch it go down.
Power-up J: the opposing side's stick is reversed.
The music fade: added to the volume every 64 frames once $73 runs out; 0 no fade.
Frames before the fade starts.
Counts 112 passes down to the next step of the match clock.
The time bar as drawn, 0-40: it fills at kick-off, then follows $76 down; full time when it is back to 0.
The time left, in bars: 40 at the start, 13 for extra time, one off every 112 passes. The interrupt sets it to $FF when CIA 2's timer B is stopped, and a match then never ends.
Passes left in the pause after a goal, 160 at the goal; kick-off at 0.
Passes left in the pause at full time, 160; the match ends at 0.
The number of entries in the menu on screen.
Set when F3 quits a match: no shop and no result.
Passes after a throw before anyone can pick the ball up.
The slot the load is for: 0 league, 1 knockout, 2 two player.
The KERNAL's status byte, and the start of $90-$C4, which the save code keeps at $BF80 while the KERNAL runs and puts back after.
The KERNAL's flag for a byte waiting to go out on the serial bus; cleared before a save or load.
The KERNAL's byte waiting to go out on the serial bus; cleared before a save or load.
The KERNAL's message switch; 0, no messages.
The KERNAL's serial end-of-data flag; cleared before a save or load.
The KERNAL's end address for SAVE, low byte: the game sets $2000, one past the saved block.
High byte of the save's end address.
The KERNAL's file name length: 3 for a save ("@:" and the digit), 1 for a load.
The KERNAL's secondary address: 1, so a load goes back to the address it was saved from.
The KERNAL's device number: 8, the disk drive.
The KERNAL's pointer to the file name: $BFFD for a save, $BFFF for a load.
High byte of the file name's address.
The KERNAL's start address for SAVE, low byte: the game sets $1C00.
High byte of the save's start address.
The KERNAL's load address, low byte: set to $1C00, though secondary address 1 makes the load use the file's own.
High byte of the load address.
Two bytes: music_init's pointer to each voice's order list in turn while it starts a tune, to fetch the list's first pattern address.
High byte of music_init's order list pointer.

The picture beside the SELECT GAME menu, an armoured player's legs, twelve rows of 96 bitmap bytes (twelve cells across, $0200-$067F) that logo_draw copies to the bitmap at $6840. The load leaves it at $6000-$64B1; file7_move moves it here, a page at a time, before the bitmap screen is first used. These are its first bytes.
The KERNAL's RS-232 enable byte, which its disk routines look at. Here it is a byte of the menu picture, so kernal_enter keeps it at $BFD8 and clears it, and kernal_leave puts it back.
The menu picture's second page, as file7_move writes it from $6100.
The KERNAL's STOP vector, low byte, inside the menu picture: kernal_enter keeps it at $BFD9 and points the vector at $EB42 while the KERNAL runs, and kernal_leave puts the picture's byte back.
The STOP vector's high byte, kept at $BFDA in the same way; then the rest of the picture's second page.
The menu picture's third page, as file7_move writes it from $6200.
The menu picture's fourth page, from $6300.
The last $B2 bytes file7_move copies, from $6400: the end of the picture, then its colours.
The menu picture's colours in the bitmap's colour screen, five by five cells (block 19, drawn at $5D08).
The menu picture's colour RAM, five by five cells (block 20, drawn at $D908).

Starts tune A (0-6): stops anything playing (music_stop_all), clears the three voices' records ($08D0, $08F4, $0918, $24 bytes each), takes the tune's tempo and each voice's order list from its seven bytes at $131E, points each voice at the first pattern of its list, sets the default arpeggio ($0E6F) and a global transpose of 0, clears the SID (sid_clear), and turns the music and all three voices on ($093C, $093E-$0940 = $FF).

Voice 1's effect flags for the note playing, cleared at each new note: bit 0 flips every frame; $04 slide down, $20 slide up, $03 the drum (noise on alternate frames), $10 an arpeggio was chosen. Each voice's record is $24 bytes: voice 2's is at $08F4 and voice 3's at $0918, and the code reaches them with X = 0, $24 or $48.
Two bytes: where voice 1 is reading in its pattern.
High byte of voice 1's pattern pointer.
Two bytes: the start of voice 1's order list, the list of its patterns' addresses ending with 0.
High byte of voice 1's order list.
Two bytes: the offset of voice 1's next order-list entry; back to 2 when the list ends and the tune repeats.
High byte of voice 1's order-list offset.
Two bytes: how far voice 1's slide has moved its frequency, added or taken off each frame.
High byte of voice 1's slide.
Two bytes: voice 1's arpeggio table, semitones added to the note frame by frame ($0E6F, $0E70 or $0E72; command $C0-$C2).
High byte of voice 1's arpeggio table.
Voice 1's place in its arpeggio table; $FF after an entry with bit 7 set, so it starts again.
Two bytes: voice 1's slide, added to $08D7 each frame (commands $84 and $85).
High byte of voice 1's slide step.
Voice 1's slide delay: counted down each frame before the test (dec, then bne), so a delay of N applies the slide first on the Nth frame, N-1 frames after the command.
Tempo steps left of voice 1's note; at 0 the next is read from the pattern (music_step).
Voice 1's note length in tempo steps, set by a byte $E0-$FF in the pattern (its low five bits plus one).
Voice 1's note, 0-$7F semitones, before the arpeggio and the transposes.
Voice 1's attack and decay, written to $D405 (pattern command $D0-$DF, or 0 for a rest).
Voice 1's sustain and release, written to $D406.
Two bytes: voice 1's frequency this frame, written to $D400/$D401.
High byte of voice 1's frequency.
Two bytes: voice 1's pulse width, written to $D402/$D403.
High byte of voice 1's pulse width.
Set by a new note: the frame's write turns voice 1's gate off and on again, restarting its envelope. A rest or a tied note leaves it clear.
Voice 1's vibrato depth (command $89).
Voice 1's vibrato speed, the step its position moves each frame.
Voice 1's vibrato position, swinging between 0 and twice the depth.
Voice 1's vibrato: $40 on (commands $89 and $82, off with $81), $20 the swing going down.
Voice 1's pulse sweep's lower limit, a high byte (command $90).
Voice 1's pulse sweep's upper limit, a high byte.
Voice 1's pulse sweep's step.
Voice 1's pulse sweep: 1 widening, $80 narrowing, 0 off (command $8F fixes the width).
Voice 1's waveform: $10 triangle, $20 sawtooth, $40 pulse, $80 noise (commands $8A-$8D), $14 triangle with ring modulation ($92).
Voice 1's waveform this frame, written to $D404 with the gate bit added; $80 on the drum's alternate frames.
Voice 1's transpose in semitones (command $97).
Voice 2's effect flags, the start of its $24-byte record; music_init clears the three records through this address and $08D0 and $0918.
Two bytes: where voice 2 is reading in its pattern.
High byte of voice 2's pattern pointer.
Two bytes: the start of voice 2's order list.
High byte of voice 2's order list.
Voice 2's offset into its order list.
Two bytes: voice 2's arpeggio table, $0E6F at the start of a tune.
High byte of voice 2's arpeggio table.
Tempo steps left of voice 2's note; 1 at the start, so the first is read at once.
Voice 2's attack and decay, for $D40C.
Voice 2's sustain and release, for $D40D.
Two bytes: voice 2's frequency this frame, for $D407/$D408.
High byte of voice 2's frequency.
Two bytes: voice 2's pulse width, for $D409/$D40A.
High byte of voice 2's pulse width.
Voice 2's envelope restart for a new note.
Voice 2's waveform this frame, for $D40B.
Voice 3's effect flags, the start of its $24-byte record.
Two bytes: where voice 3 is reading in its pattern.
High byte of voice 3's pattern pointer.
Two bytes: the start of voice 3's order list.
High byte of voice 3's order list.
Voice 3's offset into its order list.
Two bytes: voice 3's arpeggio table.
High byte of voice 3's arpeggio table.
Tempo steps left of voice 3's note.
Voice 3's attack and decay, for $D413.
Voice 3's sustain and release, for $D414.
Two bytes: voice 3's frequency this frame, for $D40E/$D40F.
High byte of voice 3's frequency.
Two bytes: voice 3's pulse width, for $D410/$D411.
High byte of voice 3's pulse width.
Voice 3's envelope restart for a new note.
Voice 3's waveform this frame, for $D412.
Not 0 while a tune plays; music_stop_all clears it.
Not 0 while a sound effect plays on voices 1 and 3.
Not 0 while the music owns voice 1; a sound effect takes it and gives it back.
Not 0 while the music owns voice 2; the launcher's hum takes it.
Not 0 while the music owns voice 3.
Not 0 while the launcher's hum plays on voice 2.
The master volume, written to $D418 each frame; the fade steps it down.
The tune's tempo, kept so tune_play can put it back in the operand at $0954.
Twice the vibrato's depth, the top of its swing, for the voice being worked on.
Two bytes: the vibrato's offset from the note, signed, scaled up by the note's octave before it is added to the frequency.
High byte of the vibrato offset.
One frame of sound, from the raster interrupt: the music (music_frame_voices), then the sound effects (effects_frame).

With music playing: adds the tempo to its running total ($0957), and on each carry steps every voice's pattern (music_step); every frame works each voice's arpeggio, slide, vibrato and pulse (music_voice_frame), and writes the voices the music owns to the SID, and the volume.
The operand of LDA #: the tune's tempo, set by music_init.
The operand of ADC #: the running total the tempo is added to each frame; a carry is a step.

The pattern commands' routines, two bytes each, for the bytes $80-$97: $80 rest, $81 vibrato off, $82 vibrato on, $84 slide down, $85 slide up, $88 next pattern, $89 vibrato, $8A-$8D a waveform, $8E drum, $8F pulse width, $90 pulse sweep, $91 end of the tune, $92 ring modulation, $94 global transpose, $95 tie, $97 transpose; $83, $86, $87, $93 and $96 are 0. Low byte first: the command's low seven bits times two index it.
The high bytes of the pattern commands' routines.
Command $88, a pattern's end: the voice's next pattern from its order list; at a 0 entry the list starts again. Then reads on.
Command $80: a rest. Attack, decay, sustain and release to 0, no envelope restart; then the note's length.
Command $95: the next note follows without restarting the envelope.
Command $94: the next byte is a transpose for every voice, stored in the operand at $0C65.
Command $97: the next byte is this voice's transpose ($08F3).
Command $90: three bytes, the pulse sweep's lower and upper limits and its step, and the sweep starts widening.
Command $8A: noise waveform.
Command $8B: pulse waveform.
Command $8C: sawtooth waveform.
Command $8D: triangle waveform.
Command $92: triangle with ring modulation ($14).
Command $8F: the next byte is the pulse width's high byte, low byte 0, and the sweep stops.
Command $91, the end of a tune that does not repeat: drops music_step's return address, so the frame's music ends here, and stops everything (music_stop_all).
Command $85: slide up. The flag $20, then as cmd_slide_down.
Command $84: slide down (flag $04): three bytes, the slide's step (two) and its delay in frames; the slide so far back to 0.
Command $89: two bytes, the vibrato's speed and depth; its position starts at the depth, and the vibrato is on.
Command $82: the vibrato on again with the speed and depth it had.
Command $81: the vibrato off.
Command $8E: the drum (flags $03): on alternate frames the voice plays noise, with $30 added to its frequency's high byte.

One tempo step for voice X: counts its note down, and when it ends clears its flags and reads the pattern: $00-$7F a note (envelope restart, its length), $80-$BF a command (music_command), $C0-$CF an arpeggio, $D0-$DF two bytes of attack-decay and sustain-release, $E0-$FF the length of the notes that follow. Commands and settings are read until a note.
The operand of JMP at $0C3B: the command's routine, from command_table.
High byte of the command's routine.

One frame of voice X: the note plus its arpeggio entry, the global transpose ($0C65) and the voice's own as an index into the frequency table ($0DC3); then the vibrato, the slide after its delay, the pulse sweep between its limits, the drum, and the frequency for the SID write.
The operand of ADC #: the transpose added to every voice's notes (command $94).
The frequency table, two bytes a note, low byte first: $0DC3-$0E68, 83 semitones from C1 (556, about 32.7 Hz) upward, in the SID's units on the PAL machine.
The high bytes of the frequency table.

Low bytes of the three arpeggio tables, for the bytes $C0-$C2 in a pattern; the high bytes follow at $0E6C, and the tables at $0E6F-$0E79. $0E6F holds $80, the plain note; $0E70 holds 0 and $8C, the note and its octave in turn; $0E72 holds 12 and seven 0s, the last with bit 7 set, so the note jumps an octave for one frame in eight. A byte with bit 7 set ends a table, its low seven bits the last entry.
High bytes of the three arpeggio tables.

Sound effect A, 0-25: takes voices 1 and 3 from the music and silences them, copies the effect's 20 bytes (effect_table) to $12C8, and starts both voices on its frequencies, envelopes, waveforms and pulse widths.
The copy loop: its LDA's operand ($0EA8) is set to the effect's record.
The operand of LDA abs,X at $0EA7: the effect's record.
High byte of the effect's record.

The addresses of the sound effects' records, two bytes each, low byte first, for effects 0-25 ($0F16-$0F49); then the 26 records, 20 bytes each, $0F4A-$1151: length in frames, step length, voice 1's and voice 3's starting frequencies, attack-decays, waveforms and pulse widths, each voice's slide and its direction, the repeat count, and a flag for a random pitch on each repeat. Known uses: 0 the ball taken, 1 a throw, 3 a tile, 5 a dome, $0F a wall, $12 the countdown, $16 a warp tunnel, $19 full time.
The high bytes of the effects' record addresses.

The 26 sound effects, 20 bytes each ($0F4A-$1151), in the order of effect_table's pointers. Starting an effect copies its record whole to $12C8-$12DB (effect_length to effect_random): the length and step, the start frequencies, envelopes, waveforms and pulse widths of voices 1 and 3, their slides and directions, the repeat count and the random flag.
The sound effect records continued, from two bytes into record 9 to the end of record 25 ($1151).
Starts voice 2's hum again from where it is: used when an effect ends while the hum plays.
The launcher's hum on voice 2 (sound_play with $FE): frequency $0280, pulse waveform, sustain 12; the music gives up voice 2.
The launcher's hum off (sound_play with $FF): voice 2's envelope to 0 and back to the music.
A sound effect is over: its voices silenced and given back to the music.
One frame of the hum while it plays: voice 2's frequency, $20 higher on frames when two random bits are clear, so it warbles, and its pulse width moving on each frame.

One frame of effects, after stepping the random generator: an effect playing counts its length down; at the end of each step it puts the frequencies back to their start (adding a random number to voice 1's high byte if flagged) until its repeats run out; within a step it slides voice 1 and voice 3 each frame. Then the hum.
The effect playing: frames left; at 0 the effect ends. The first of the 20 bytes copied from the effect's record.
Frames in each step of the effect.
Two bytes: voice 1's frequency at the start of each step.
High byte of voice 1's starting frequency.
Two bytes: voice 3's frequency at the start of each step.
High byte of voice 3's starting frequency.
Voice 1's attack and decay for the effect.
Voice 3's attack and decay.
Voice 1's waveform for the effect.
Voice 3's waveform.
Voice 1's pulse width's high byte.
Voice 3's pulse width's high byte.
Two bytes: voice 1's frequency change each frame.
High byte of the effect's voice 1 slide, as the effect record sets it.
Two bytes: voice 3's frequency change each frame.
High byte of voice 3's slide.
Voice 1's slide: 0 none, positive up, negative down.
Voice 3's slide: 0 none, positive up, negative down.
Steps left that put the frequencies back to their start; at 0 the voices keep their last frequency until the length runs out.
Not 0: each step adds a random number to voice 1's starting frequency's high byte.
Frames left of this step.
Two bytes: voice 1's frequency now.
High byte of voice 1's frequency now.
Two bytes: voice 3's frequency now.
High byte of voice 3's frequency now.
The hum's frequency, low byte ($80 at the start).
The hum's frequency, high byte (2).
The hum's pulse width, low byte, growing each frame.
The hum's pulse width, high byte.
Stops the music, the effects and the hum, and clears the SID (sid_clear).
Writes 0 to every SID register $D400-$D417, then the volume to $D418.
Steps the driver's own random generator, a 32-bit shift register at $131A-$131D, and returns its top byte.
The random generator's top byte, the one returned.
The random generator's second byte.
The random generator's third byte.
The random generator's low byte.

Seven bytes for each of the tunes 0-6: the tempo, then the three voices' order lists. Tune 0 the menu, 1 the prematch screens, 2 the league table after a win or a draw, 3 after a loss, 4 the team choice, 5 a goal for side 0 and the end of a match, 6 a goal for side 1.
Voice 1's order list for each tune (two bytes, tune * 7 + 1).
Tune 0's header, byte 2: the high byte of its voice 1 order list. music_init reads each tune's voice 2 low byte through this address, with X one past the header's start.
Voice 2's order list for each tune.
Tune 0's header, byte 4: the high byte of its voice 2 order list. music_init reads voice 3's low byte through this address.
Voice 3's order list for each tune.

Tune 0's order lists, the addresses of its patterns in the order they play, each list ending with 0: voice 1's $134F-$13E6 (75 entries), voice 3's $13E7-$1470 (68), voice 2's $1471-$14A0 (23). A pattern is notes, lengths, settings and commands (music_step), ending with $88.
Tune 0's ten patterns for voice 1, $14A1-$1664.
Tune 0's six patterns for voice 3, $1665-$16D4.
A pattern no order list names: note $20 twelve times and $88.
Tune 0's eight patterns for voice 2, $16E6-$1873.
Tune 1, the prematch screens' tune: its order lists ($1874-$188D) and its patterns ($188E-$18F9).
Tune 2, after a league match won or drawn: order lists $18FA-$1911 and patterns $1912-$1971.
Tune 3, after a league match lost: order lists $1972-$1989 and patterns $198A-$19EF.
Tune 4, the team choice: order lists $19F0-$19FB and patterns $19FC-$1AE0.
Tune 5, a goal for side 0 and the end of a match: order lists $1AE1-$1AEC and patterns $1AED-$1B24.
Tune 6, a goal for side 1: order lists $1B25-$1B2C (voice 2 shares tune 5's) and patterns $1B2D-$1B66.

The loader jumps here when every file is in memory. JMP to the start-up at $201A, then four more jumps: $2003 and $2006 to $6000 and $6048, which no code calls (at run time $6000 holds a bitmap, at the hand-over the block the start-up copies to $0200); $2009 the save routine and $200C the load routine, which the menu calls.
JMP save_game ($BD50): the SAVE GAME entry calls it with the file's digit in A.
JMP load_game ($BD70): the three LOAD entries call it with the slot number in A.

Waits 256 frames: Y is set to 0 and wait_frame ($B179) called until it counts back round to 0; then it clears the carry, sets it again, and returns. No code found calls it, directly or through a table.

Start-up, run once. Interrupts off, $01 = $0D (RAM at $A000 and $E000, the chips in), waits for raster line $FB, blacks the border and backgrounds, blanks the screen, selects video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF), sprites off and all multicolour. Stops CIA 1's interrupts, points the NMI and reset vectors at $8703 (an RTI) and the IRQ vector at irq_handler ($86D3), clears zero page $02-$FF, fills the sprite order list $1E-$2D with 0-15, arms the raster interrupt at line $28 with slot 5, seeds the random generator ($32/$33 = $19, $63), and starts CIA 2's timers A and B, period $231F, with their interrupts masked: two stores four cycles apart, the gap the protection checks rely on (irq_slot_play_top). Then all RAM ($01 = $30), the block at $6000 copied to $0200 (file7_move), and on to the menu (main_menu_boot).

Re-entry from a prematch screen's F3 (prematch_wait), stack reset: the menu with "continue" possible (menu_resume); if a game is under way or was loaded ($1EE9) it goes on with it at match_restart, otherwise to new_game_reset.
From start-up: no game in progress (game type $1EAF = $80), then main_menu.
The top of the game, stack reset: the SELECT GAME menu (menu_main), whose entries set up a game and return here. A loaded or unfinished game ($1EE9) goes on at match_restart.

A new game: round $1EC4, both sides' tokens ($1EB1, $1EB2), the bribed goals ($1EF0, $1EF1) and the pitch layout counter $1ED0 to 0, the bought handicaps cleared (handicap_clear), both power-up durations ($1EC7, $1EC8) 120 passes and the countdown paces ($1EC9, $1ECA) 12.
Clears the knockout round's points and legs ($1EC2, $1EC3), then match_start.
A new match: 40 bars on the clock target ($76), no extra time ($1EDC), both scores 0.

The start of a match or of its extra time: the drawn clock bar $75 at 0, the quit flag $7A clear, the clock's pass counter $74 at 112. By game type ($1EAF): a league loads this week's opponent (opponent_load, record = week) and shows the league prematch screen; a knockout takes the template number $1CD1 of record round + 1 and loads the record with that number (a second lookup, so the figures are another team's than the one the screen names), then its screen; a two player game its own. Then the players' stamina and power (players_attributes_set) and the pitch (pitch_setup).

Every kick-off, after a goal too: music stopped (tune 0 when $53 is set), the goal countdown $77, ball holder, thrower, flight, height, throw counters, the computer's timers and both ball speeds cleared; friction pace $1EDF = 14, throw strength $1EE0 = 7, flight $1EEF = 26; power-ups cleared (effects_clear) and the next tile in 50 passes ($67); the ball to the launcher, any bribed goals ($1EF0, $1EF1) added to the scores, the scores drawn, every player to his start (players_reset_all), and the ball launcher (launcher_sequence).

One pass of play, after a frame wait. With RUN/STOP held ($56) the game pauses until fire on port 2 (or port 1 in a two player game). F3 ($55), unless full time is already counting, quits the match (match_quit). During the goal countdown ($77) the players walk back to their places (players_walk_home) and the ball slides to the centre (ball_slide_home), and at its end comes the kick-off. During the full-time countdown ($78) the same, tune 5 at step 80, and at its end match_over. Otherwise the clock (clock_step), and full time when its drawn bar is back to 0; then the players (players_update), the ball (ball_move: a goal goes to goal_scored), the ball's sprite, stamina meters, tiles, pick-ups for both sides.

The rest of every pass: flags a sprite update ($4F), waits a frame, counts $62, the tile (tile_step), the launcher's lift (launcher_lift), the power-up countdown, the ball-holder markers in the panel (holder_markers), the scroll (scroll_update), then match_loop again.
A goal: the scores drawn, the tile removed, the 160-pass countdown ($77), and tune 5 when the ball went in at the top ($1E48 = 0, side 0 scored) or tune 6 at the bottom.
F3 during a match: sets the quit flag $7A and falls into time_up.
Full time: the 160-pass countdown ($78), the tile removed, and sound $19.

The full-time countdown is over: music stopped, the play sprites saved back to $F300 (play_sprites_out). A quit match goes straight to the menu. Otherwise the token shop (match_result_shop); a draw with extra time bought ($1EDC) restarts with 13 bars on the clock. Then by game type: a league plays out the week (league_week_end), moves the week $1ED8 on (1 again after 11, with the week count $1EDB and the season $1EC4, ending the league at $1EB0 with league_over_screen); a knockout scores the leg (knockout_round_end: next leg, next round, or out); a two player game records the match (twoplayer_week_end). The pitch layout $1ED0 moves on, 0-9.

The match clock, once a pass: every 112 passes ($74) the target $76 comes down one bar, and each pass the drawn bar $75 moves one step toward it, so it fills from 0 to 40 at kick-off and then empties as time runs; match_loop calls full time when it is back to 0. Draws the bar into the ten cells at $7381: full cells (character 8) up to its end, the end cell 9-12 by quarter, and all ten full at 40.
Takes the tile off the pitch (tile_floor_put), sets the tile delay $67 to 255, and falls into effects_clear.
Ends every power-up: $6B (P), $6C (F), $6D (R), $70 (W) and $71 (J) cleared, the countdown $1ECC stopped, and the launcher objects hidden (launcher_objects_hide).

Puts the floor back where the tile was: block 13's source is the floor piece at $21F7/$21F9 (the second one when the tile's column $69 is 3 or more and its row $6A 2 or more), drawn by block_put; $4A = $FF makes the next pass redraw the screen.
Sets up objects 10-13, the parts of the ball launcher, from row Y of the table at $2D21: x ($2D21, $2D29), y ($2D31, $2D39), colour ($2D41), sprite pointer ($2D49) and multicolour flag ($2D51).
Hides objects 10-13 by setting their y high bytes ($1E33-$1E36, $1E43-$1E46) to $80.

Once a pass. While the tile delay $67 runs it counts down, and at 0 a new tile appears: its cell chosen (tile_place) and its type (tile_choose), and block 13 drawn there from $DBF9 (characters $F8-$FB). While a tile is on the pitch its four characters at $7FC0-$7FDF are redrawn each pass from the type's patterns at $DC3D and $DC5D, one byte further on ($66), so the pattern rolls. Then the power-up time $1ECD counts down, and at 0 every power-up ends (effects_clear).
Each side's stamina and power into its five players: $1EB7 and $1EB5 into $1CE7 and $1CF1 for players 0-4, $1EB8 and $1EB6 into $1CEC and $1CF6 for players 5-9.
Every player to his start (player_reset, with $41 = $FF), and players 4 and 9 the controlled ones ($60, $61).

Player X back to his start: facing ($2DE3), action 2, $1D05 from $2DED, position from $2E01 (x) and $2E0B/$2E15 (y), role from $2DD9 and sprite pointer from $2DF7, and $1D2D, his flags, $1D69 and $1D5F cleared.
During a countdown: each player steps toward his start ($2E01, $2E0B, $2E15) and, once there, faces his start way and stops (flags $10 and $40 cleared).
For the five players from X: the distance to the ball, in units of 4 pixels (distance_approx), into $1D41. Clears $7B.
The player of the four from X with the smallest $1D41: the one nearest the ball.
The stick bits that take player X toward the target ($39-$3E) from where he is ($37-$3C), in $41 (dir_to_target).

Stick bits (1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right) from the position in $37/$3B, $38/$3C toward the target $39/$3D, $3A/$3E: 0 when both differences are under 6; a single direction when one difference is at least 20 more than the other; a diagonal otherwise.
Subtracts the 16-bit value at $39+Y-2 ($37+Y, $3B+Y) from the one at $37+X ($3B+X): the difference of two coordinates.
Negates the 16-bit coordinate difference at $37+X, $3B+X.
Carry set when the difference at $37+X is 6 or more.
Carry set when the difference at $37+X is 20 ($14) or more.
Sprite colours: players 0-4 green (5), 5-9 red (2). Unless a countdown is running, every fourth frame ($62 bit 2) the controlled players show light green ($0D) and light red ($0A).

The ball launcher at a kick-off: waits for it to rise (launcher_lift, $1EF3), puts the ball on it at ($94, $0E low bytes), starts its sound ($FE), sets up its parts (launcher_objects_set, row 3) and spins it a random 16-48 turns: its direction $19 steps round the eight directions, shown as the ball's sprite (launcher_frame), with sprite multicolour 0 flashed at the raster lines in $BB2C. Then shoots the ball out in the last direction at a random strength 1-4 ($BA61, $BAB1), sounds $FF and 0, hides the launcher, puts the ball back on the centre, lets the camera follow, and lowers the launcher ($1EF3 = $FF).
The ball's sprite shows the launcher's arrow: pointer $7A + direction $19, colour 15, and a sprite update flagged.
The ball's sprite by its height: pointer from $2D69 at the height phase |$1EE3|, colour 15. Under power-up W ($70) the ball is the electric one: pointer $37, colour light red.

One pass of the ball. Held ($1EE1), it sits at the holder's feet: his position plus the offset for his facing ($BB01/$BB09, $BB11/$BB19), on the ground. Free: its height phase steps up to 7 and back down through -7 to 0 ($1EE3, a step every $1EE4 passes); still for 120 passes, it is shot off in a random direction at strength $1EE0. Side walls at x $1C and $108 bounce it (sound $0F) unless it is on the ground in the warp tunnels (y $108-$127, tunnel_check), which send it out of the other side (sound $16). At the top (y below $18) and bottom (y $228 on) a ball on the ground between x $64 and $C7 (goal_check) is a goal: side 0's score $1EAD or side 1's $1EAE goes up, the ball is put back in front of the goal, and it returns 1; otherwise it bounces. On the ground it can hit a dome (dome_bounce). Every 14 passes ($1EDF) friction takes a step off each speed; then the speeds are added to the position.

During a countdown, the ball slides 2 pixels a pass toward line $118. The test that should stop it there compares the position's high byte with $18, so it never matches; ball_to_launcher, the snap it was meant to make, is reached only through the other branch's end.
Puts the ball on the centre spot: x $A0, y $118.
Returns 1 when the ball is on the ground (height phase 0) between x $64 and $C7, the goal mouth.
Returns 1 when the ball is on the ground with y between $108 and $127, in front of a warp tunnel.
Reverses the ball's horizontal speed $1EDD.
Reverses the ball's vertical speed $1EDE.

41 bytes of code that no instruction or table reaches: a tunnel check for any object Y, without the ground test (1 when its y is $108-$127, sharing tunnel_check's exits), then two routines that negate $2D59,Y and $2D5D,Y.

Whether a side 0 player picks up the free ball: nobody holds it, the throw's pick-up delay $7B is over; the thrower ($1EE2) cannot take it back until $1EEF runs out. A player within 3 units ($1D41), not marked $80, takes it; a ball in the air only by one jumping (action 1, at frame 2 or later, other than 6). The keeper (role 0) throws it straight back up the pitch at once; the top keeper (player 5) down it; any other player takes it (ball_take_side0, ball_take_side1).
The same for side 1's players 5-9.

Side 0's player X takes the ball. Under side 1's power-up W ($70 negative) the ball bounces off him instead and he goes down (action 5); that path also adds $2DD0 into the text counts at $2469, a corruption that only a copy with mismatched timers suffers. Side 1's player X takes the ball: the same, with side 0's W ($70 = 1) bouncing it, $61 the controlled player, $1EC5 = $FF and the formation $1EB4.
The bottom keeper throws the ball straight up the pitch: sound 1, sideways speed by his facing (throw_speed_set), up at the throw strength $1EE0, facing up; then keeper_throw.
The top keeper throws it down the pitch: straight in a one player game, by his facing in a two player game.
The rest of a keeper's throw: flight counters $1EEF and $7B at 26, friction pace 12, a lob (height phase 1, step 6), the keeper as the thrower, nobody holding, and action 3.
The menu with a game under way ($1EE9 = 1), then menu_loop.
The menu with no game kept ($1EE9 = 0).
Tune 0, eight entries ($79), the box twelve rows high ($2363), the SELECT GAME menu (menu_select, text group 0), then a jump to the chosen entry's handler through $2283/$228B.
ONE PLAYER KNOCKOUT: the eleven teams' records (knockout_init) and game type 1, then menu_teams.

The team choice (team_select), nothing kept; the sides' attributes set by game type (side_attributes_set, both_attributes_set) and, for a league or a two player game, the league's length (league_length_menu).
TWO PLAYER GAME: the records (league_init), game type 0, then menu_teams.
ONE PLAYER LEAGUE: the records (league_teams_init), game type $FF, then menu_teams.

SAVE GAME, when a game is in progress: a screen of instructions (box 12, text group 16), fire to go on or F3 to give up; then box 13, text group $14, the save (jv_save_game) of the file for this game type ($2293: "0" league, "1" knockout, "2" two player), text group $15 or $18 by the carry, and a wait for fire.
LOAD LEAGUE: slot $2DD0 (0 on a genuine copy), then menu_load.
LOAD KNOCKOUT: slot 1.
LOAD TWO PLAYER GAME: slot 2.

One side's choice among the three teams, the one already taken ($1ED1) skipped: text group 6, the cursor $1EE8 moved by left and right with a ten-frame repeat; fire plays the chosen team's animation (frames from $B95F/$B969 by the lists at $2EEB, $2EEE and $2EF1, into the picture at $2F2D/$2F30, five 8-byte columns, four frames apart). Six slow ticks ($11) with no input go back to the menu.
Side 0's stamina, power and tackle figure ($1EB7, $1EB5, $1EB9) from team $1ED1's entries at $B9D6, $B9D9 and $B9DC.
Both sides': side 0's as above, side 1's ($1EB8, $1EB6, $1EBA) from team $1ED2.
The eleven team records 10 down to 0 from the eleven templates (team_record_init), week $1ED8 = 1, $1EDB = 2.

Team record X from template Y: the template number ($1CD1), power ($1C4D from $BA16), stamina ($1C58 from $BA0B), $1C63 ($B9DF), $1C6E ($B9EA), keeper delay ($1C79 from $B9F5), $1C84 ($BA00), tackle figure ($1CA5 from $BA21); goals, points, matches, wins, losses and draws cleared.
The computer's side from team record Y: power $1EB6, stamina $1EB8, $1EBB, $1EBC, keeper delay $1EBD, $1EBE and $1EBF, and the tackle figure $1EBA; then the bought handicaps (attributes_handicap).

After a match: side 0's token shop, then in a two player game side 1's, with the screen blanked between; extra time bought ($1EDC) counts down one; waits for fire to be released.

Sprites 0-11, hires: 0 empty; 1-3 the SELECT GAME highlight bar's left end, middle and right end; 4-7 the four corners of the frame round the team being chosen; 8 and 9 two corner pieces; 10 a bar, which slot 9 repeats across the prematch screens; 11 a block of upright stripes.

In a match, sprite $74, the end of the throw to the right, and $75-$77, a throw to the left. On the menus, the colour screen's second page.

Inside sprite $78; on the menus, the second mark.
Inside sprite $78; on the menus, the third mark.

The SELECT GAME menu and its cursor. Clears the bitmap screen (screen_off_clear), puts the side's number in the heading ($2816 = $81 + side) and draws text group 6, the side's team picture (team_panel_draw; recoloured for side 1 by panel_recolour), clears boxes 9 and 3, draws the token bar (token_bar_draw), clears the bought flags (shop_clear_bought) and draws the price list (shop_list_draw). Uses sprite block $28 with the cursor on item 0 and the shop's interrupt chain (slot 3). Then once a frame reads the side's stick: up and down move the cursor to the next item that is not crossed out, wrapping between 0 and 10; fire on item 0 leaves the shop; fire on any other marks it bought, takes its price ($2C23) from the side's tokens ($1EB1), runs its effect through the table at $BB83/$BBA1 (Y = this side, X = the other), and redraws the token bar and the list.

Scores a knockout leg from $1EAD and $1EAE: two points ($1EC2) for a win, one for a draw, and one more leg played ($1EC3). Three points or more win the round: the round number $1EC4 moves on and, after round 10, the tournament is won (knockout_won_screen) and it returns $FF; otherwise 1. With fewer points, three legs played, or two legs with no points, the team is out (knockout_lost_screen) and it returns $FF. Otherwise 0, play the next leg.

Records a two player match in the league table (league_record, teams 0 and 1) and moves the week counter $1ED8 on, back to 1 after 10, at which point the round counter $1EC4 moves on; when it reaches the length chosen ($1EB0) the final table is shown (twoplayer_final) and it returns 1, otherwise 0.

The end of a two player league: shows the table screen (prematch_screen_setup), text group 12 and box 8, both team cards, and the winner's picture: the team with more points ($1C8F/$1C9A of teams 0 and 1; side 1's picture is recoloured), then waits for fire.
The end of a one player league: the side's picture, box 8 cleared, text group 10, waits for fire and shows the final table (league_table_screen).
Knockout won: the side's picture, box 6 cleared, text group 8, then waits for fire.
Knocked out: the side's picture, box 5 cleared, text group 7, then waits for fire.

The KNOCKOUT ROUND screen before each leg: the screen set up (prematch_screen_setup), tune 1, the round number as a digit ($80 + $1EC4) in the text at $2828, text group 11, the opponent ($1ED7 = round + 1) drawn by prematch_draw. Returns at once when that says to play; otherwise redraws the cards and waits again (prematch_wait) until fire or F3.

The two player screen before each match: the screen set up, tune 1, the week number ($1ED8, two digits) written into the text at $2834, text group 12, both teams' pictures and cards, then prematch_wait until fire.

The league screen before each week's match: the screen set up, tune 1, the week number in the text at $2840, text group 13, this week's opponent ($1ED7 = week) drawn by prematch_draw, then prematch_wait.

Draws both teams on a prematch screen: side 0's picture and card (left_team_draw), the frame at panel 2 (panel_frame), the opponent's face ($1CD1 of team $1ED7, panel_face_draw) and card (opponent_card_draw), and falls into prematch_messages.

The line under the teams: box $2468 (0 on a genuine copy, see irq_slot_play_top), "extra time" (box 1) after a drawn match with a bribe, else in a knockout the leg (the text at $2A48 = "1"-"3", box 2) and the score so far (box 3 + points after a first leg; boxes 6 or 7 after a second), then shows the screen (screen_on) and falls into prematch_wait.

Waits up to 128 frames ($10) for fire on port 2 (returns 0) or F3 ($55, back to the menu through main_menu_resume). When the time runs out it flips $1EEE, which the card routines read to swap between the team's card and its attributes, and returns 1 so the caller redraws.
Side 0's team picture (team_panel_draw with X = 0, team $1ED1), its frame (panel_frame, X = 1) and the face area (face_box_draw), then its card (left_card_draw).

Side 0's card under its picture: the team's name, captain and attributes. In a game other than a knockout, while $1EEE is set, the team's name and league line instead (team_line_draw). Sets $1EF5 = 0.
Writes the card text for team Y (team_text_set) and the attribute numbers (attributes_text_set), then falls into card_rows_draw.

Draws seven rows of twelve characters from the text at ($12) into the screen at the address from $23B4/$23B7 (X = 0 or 2: left or right card), each character through the font table $2BA0; the screen pointer moves 40 cells a row, the text 12.
Side 1's picture (team $1ED2) on the right, recoloured (panel_recolour), then falls into right_card_draw.
Side 1's card ($1EF5 = 1): team card, or the league line while $1EEE is set.
The computer opponent's card on the right (team $1ED7): the league line in a league while $1EEE is set, otherwise its card with $1EF5 = 1.

A team's league line on a card: the text at $2B6C filled with the team's name (from $303C via the index at $3020, spaces dropped) and its row of figures from the league table (league_row_text), then drawn by card_rows_draw.

Plays out the rest of a league week. After the human's match, each of the week's four other fixtures (from $2F9E, eight bytes a week, team numbers from 1) is decided at random: about one in twelve (a random byte $75-$89) is a draw, 0-5 goals each; otherwise a team rating difference ($1CA5) sets the odds, and the winner scores 2-9 (random_win_score). Each result goes into the table (league_record). In week 10 the human's team rests: the next week is played the same way at once, with the table shown between (league_table_screen).

The league table: tune 2 or 3 (won or lost), sorts the positions (league_rank), draws the frame of the table screen (table_frame_draw) and the eleven rows, then flashes the human's row by redrawing it blank and full every 36 frames until fire.
Copies the 40 characters of the row text at $DA69 into the screen at ($14).

The table screen: colour RAM all 9, screen $7400 characters $47 onward for the heading, ten rows of the template at $DAB9, the header rows from $DB31/$DB09/$DAE1, and colour rows from $2FF8 into colour RAM from $D878.

The one interrupt handler, for the raster interrupt only. Saves the registers and $01, banks the chips in ($01 = $0D) and, for a raster interrupt, runs the next slot of the interrupt chain (irq_slot_run). Then a check of the copy protection, written with undocumented opcodes the disassembler shows as data: LAX $DD0F / ANC #$01 reads CIA 2's control register B and keeps its start bit; when timer B is not running it sets the clock target $76 to $FF, so a match on a copy never reaches full time. Restores $01 and the registers.
RTI. The NMI and reset vectors point here, so RESTORE does nothing.

Runs slot $08 of the interrupt chain: moves $08 to the slot's successor ($2C5E), sets the next raster line ($2C52) and acknowledges, re-enables interrupts, and unless the slot's flag ($2C8E) is negative writes its $D011 (ORed with $09, the screen-on bit), $D016, $D018 and sprite enable (ANDed with $0A). Then jumps to the slot's routine through $2C3A/$2C46.

Slot 0, line $14, the top of the play screen. Sprites off; a check of the copy protection (the operands are changed by irq_slot_shop_row to random mirrors of CIA 2's timer registers): adds timer A's low byte EOR timer B's low byte to $2DD0, which the stick reading and the frame wait use, so the two timers must count in step; and adds one to $2468 when two reads of timer A's low byte agree, that is when timer A has stopped. Then sprites on, the multiplexer's slot table and sprite pointers 1-7 of both screens cleared, and the play colours (slot 5).
The low byte of the EOR $DD00 operand at $874C: set to a random $x4 by irq_slot_shop_row, so the instruction reads CIA 2's timer A low byte through one of the register mirrors.
The low byte of the EOR $DD02 operand at $874F: set to a random $x6, timer B's low byte through a mirror.
The low byte of the LDA $DD00 operand at $8759: set to a random $x4, timer A's low byte.
The low byte of the CMP $DD00 operand at $875C: set to a random $x4, timer A's low byte again, read four cycles after the LDA.

Slot 2, the score panel under the pitch (line $DB, set by the multiplexer when it is done): sprites off and moved out of the way, $D010 from $2CBF, waits for the next raster line and writes $D011 = 7 to split the screen, panel colours (slot 4), the frame's work (frame_work), and when a sprite update is pending ($4F) the camera and sprite positions (sprites_place), the sort (sprites_sort) and the ball shadow (player_colours).
Slot 3, line $FC on menu screens: loads the sprite registers from block $1EEC (sprite_block_load).
Slot 6: an RTS, a slot with nothing to do.

Slot 8, line $A0, on the screens prematch_screen_setup draws (the team choice, the prematch screens and the league table): sprites hi-res and expanded both ways; with a team highlighted ($1EE8 positive) places four sprites from $2F45/$2F59 by the entry in $2F33 and their pointers from $2F36, black; with $1EE8 negative, sprites off.

Slot 9, line $B2: a row of eight expanded black sprites (pointer $0A) at y $B2 from x positions $2F51. Then sets the four protection operands at $874D-$875D to random mirrors of CIA 2's timer low bytes ($DDx4, $DDx6).
Port 2 into $0C (bits: 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire) ORed with $2DD0; port 1 into $0D, EORed with $2468. Both are 0 on a genuine copy.

Reads three keys into $55-$57 (non-zero while held): F3 (quit, $55), RUN/STOP (pause, $56), F5 ($57), by the rows at $2CA6 and masks at $2CA9. Then a check of the copy protection in undocumented opcodes (LAX $DD4F / ANC #$01, CIA 2's control register B through a mirror): when timer B is stopped it EORs the interrupt slot number $08 with $AA, sending the chain to a slot that does not exist.
Screen and sprites on: $09 = $10 (the $D011 bit ORed in by irq_slot_run) and $0A = $FF (the sprite mask), then waits a frame.
Screen and sprites off ($09 = $0A = 0) and the blank chain (slot 5) after the next frame.
Waits a frame, then makes Y the next slot of the interrupt chain ($08).

Once a frame, from the interrupt: music and fades (music_frame), sticks and keys, the frame-wait flag $0B from $2DD0 (0, releasing wait_frame), the frame counter $0F, the slow counter $11 (down one every 256 frames) and the delay counter $10 (down one a frame).
Background colours of set Y with the chips banked in (colours_load).

Loads every sprite register from the 42-byte block at $2D72+Y: eight x/y pairs, $D010, enable, y expand, priority, multicolour, x expand, colours 0 and 1, then colours 1-7 ($2D81) and pointers 0-7 ($2D89, screen $5C00).

Slot 1, the sprite multiplexer, re-armed at line $AA and after: hands the next objects in screen order (the list at $1E, from $1C) to hardware sprites 1-7 whose last object has been drawn ($2CB7 = 0), one object at least a pass; when the list is used up goes on to the panel (slot 2 at line $DB). Otherwise sets the next interrupt 16 lines above the next object and frees each hardware sprite whose object ends above that line.

Hardware sprite X takes object Y: colour ($2CF1), pointer ($2D01, on both screens' pointer rows $77F8 and $6FF8), its y kept in $2CB7, x and y ($2CC1, $2CE1), and its bits in $D010 ($2CD1) and the multicolour register ($2D11), kept in $2CBF and $2CC0.

Works out the camera (camera_follow), the sprite y offset $4D/$4E (camera less $36), puts the ball (object 15) in hardware sprite 0, then counts in $50 the objects 0-13 whose screen y lands between $20 and $DE, setting the y of the rest to 0; $1C starts the multiplexer at the first visible.

The camera's top line $2E/$2F: the followed object's y less $54, kept between 0 and $1A8. It follows the ball, or while a player holds it ($1EE1, no countdown running) the controlled player of the holder's side ($60 or $61). Nothing while $4B is set.
Object Y's sprite x ($1E09 + $18, with $FF in $2CD1 past 255) and y less the offset ($30/$31).
Sorts the object list at $1E-$2D by sprite y ($2CE1), a bubble sort repeated until a pass makes no swap ($1EED).
Player X's sprite pointer: from the frame list for his current action ($1DA5/$1DAF), the entry for his facing ($1D0F) plus the animation step ($1D19), into $2D01.
Starts tune A (tune_play) and sets $72 and $73 to $FF: the volume steps down by one every 64 frames after a delay of 255 (music_frame).
Starts tune A: volume $0942 = 15, $0954 from $0943, and the music driver's start at $0810 with the chips banked in; no fade.
Volume 0, no fade, and the driver's stop routine ($12E5).
Plays a frame of music ($0947), and counts the fade: after $73 frames, every 64 frames adds $72 to the volume $0942 until it reaches 0.

Sound effect A. A positive number starts that effect ($0E7A) and sets the volume to 15; $FE starts the launcher's sound ($1155) at full volume; any other negative number stops it ($1190). Keeps X and Y. The test of $53 at its start would skip the effect while a tune plays, but nothing sets $53.

Bounce domes: for each of the four domes of this pitch ($1ED0 picks four entries of $2E73, $2E9B and $2EC3), whether the ball's centre lies in the dome's 32-pixel square. On a hit: sound 5, $1EE7 = 6, both ball speeds ($1EDD, $1EDE) one step faster, and the ball turned by the part of the square it is in: the top or bottom edge reverses the vertical speed (ball_bounce_y), the left or right edge the horizontal (ball_bounce_x), and a corner swaps the two speeds, negating the new vertical one at the top-left and bottom-right corners.

The two stamina meters in the panel: for each side, the stamina of its controlled player ($1CE7, at most 32 shown) as four cells at the address from $224B/$224D: full cells (8), one partial cell 9-12 by quarter, and empties (9).
For player X: whether any of the five players listed by $2F19/$2F23 within $32 of him lies in the direction he faces ($1D0F). Returns 1 if so, 0 if not.
The direction (0 up, 1 up-right, 2 right ... 7 up-left) from object Y to object X, from their x and y differences, with diagonals when the smaller difference is at least half the larger.
x of object X less x of object Y, in $45/$47.
Negates $45/$47.
Compares half the x difference with the y difference; carry set when it is larger.
Halves the y difference and compares it with the x difference; carry set when it is larger.
The smallest of entries 1-4 of the list at ($2F19/$2F23 for X).
The 16-pixel column of object X ($1E09/$1E19 / 16) looked up in $BBEF.
Swaps the roles ($1D23) of players X and Y.

Runs after pair_distances has measured the players ($4C set). Goes through the 45 pairs ($F243 and $F270 name the two; pairs 0-34 have a side 0 player first, 35-44 are side 1's players with each other) by the distance at $1E49 plus the pair's cell, read through $F290; a negative distance is a touch. A touching pair of opponents goes to tackle_resolve, once for each side 0 player a frame ($49, set again where $B973 marks the start of the next player's pairs); a touching pair of team-mates is pushed apart: a controlled player ($60, $61) back to his last position (player_pos_undo), any other knocked aside (player_bump). Because $F290 is 13 bytes before the real cell list, pairs 4-12 and 18-21 are judged by the distance of one of pairs 0-3 (player 0 with players 1-4): side 0's keeper with each of side 1's players, player 1 with 2-5 and player 2 with 4-7.
Puts object X back at the position saved before his last move ($1DB9, $1DC3, $1DCD, $1DD7).

Pair zpa_18: unless already being pushed ($1D5F), a moving player ($1D55) is pushed for 5 frames ($1D5F) in the direction from $2E33 by his facing and the direction to the other; when it is side 1's controlled player and side 0 holds the ball, a new target (ai_side1_target).

Two opponents touch (pair zpa_18; the first player is side 0's, the second side 1's). A player sliding (action 4) brings the other down when a random byte is at least the other side's tackle figure ($1EB9 or $1EBA) and that side does not have the P power-up ($6B): the victim goes down (action 5 with sound 6), loses stamina by the slider's power (stamina_drain) and takes his facing, and if he held the ball the slider takes it; the slider then gets up (action 2). A player who is down (flag $10) does not tackle. Otherwise the two facings, through the table at $B996, decide: 0 no tackle (both pushed apart), 1 the first player wins, $FF the second wins, 2 the one running (action 2) wins, or nobody when neither runs. A human-controlled player wins only while his fire is pressed ($1EC0 for side 0, $1EC1 for side 1 in a two player game). The loser goes down as above, the winner takes action 6 with flag $08, and takes the ball if the loser held it.
Player Y loses stamina ($1CE7) by player X's power ($1CF1), not below 0, and turns to face the way X faces ($1D0F).
The same the other way round: player X loses stamina by player Y's power and takes Y's facing.
The ball's horizontal speed $1EDD for a throw by player X: from $BA61 at the throw strength $1EE0 times 8 plus his facing (with $2DD0 ORed in, 0 on a genuine copy).

Builds the match screen: screen off, the play character set from $DF55 to $7800 and the panel screen from $EC0D to $7000 (block_copy 1 and 2), the sprite registers for play (play_sprites_init), the play sprites moved from $F300 to $5C00 (play_sprites_in), the camera held ($4B) on the ball's start (ball_to_launcher, camera_follow), every player on his start (players_reset_all), sprite positions and sort, both scores and $2D10 cleared, colour RAM 8, dome positions (domes_place), the pitch map (pitch_map_build), the panel (panel_draw), the first screen (scroll_update), play colours, a sprite update flagged, the play interrupt chain (slot $2DD0, 0 on a genuine copy) and the screen on.
Sprite registers for play, chips banked in: all eight on and multicolour, none expanded or behind the background, multicolours 0 (black) and 1 (white).
After a match, copies twelve pages $5C00-$67FF (the play sprites) back up to $F300-$FEFF, where they wait for the next match while the menus use $5C00.
Before a match, copies twelve pages from $F300-$FEFF down to $5C00-$67FF, sprites 112-159 of video bank 1.

The score panel's rows (panel_rows) and the stamina meters.
Both scores into the panel: $1EAD and $1EAE as decimal digits, the last two put in the panel's screen row at $7378 + the offset from $22F4.
The panel's middle row from $21FB (characters, at $7370) and $2223 (colours, at $DB70), and the rows above and below it filled with character 3 in colour 8. Chips banked in for the colour RAM.

The four domes of this match's pitch layout ($1ED0 times 4 picks the entries in $2E73, $2E9B and $2EC3): each dome's map address (row from $20E5/$212F, plus column) goes into blocks 9-12 of the block table ($21AC/$21C1), and its cell position, less 2, into $2DD1 (row) and $2DD5 (column) for the tile placing.
Starts the scroll: screen buffer $44 = 0 and last row $4A = 0, then falls into scroll_update.

Once a frame: the pitch row at the camera's top (scroll_row). When it is the same row as last time, the spare time measures the players (pair_distances); when it has changed, the map is copied into the hidden screen (the routine named by $2296/$2298 for buffer $44) and the buffers swap (screen_flip). Then the fine scroll (scroll_fine).

Swaps the screen buffer $44 and sets the play slot's $D018 ($2C82) from $229A: screen $6C00 or $7400, characters at $7800.
